title: Check yourself: what the streams contract promises

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, on which threads does a parallel stream do its work in Java 21?

options.says: The page says parallel streams do not use virtual threads, and points virtual threads at I/O-bound work instead.

options.text: On platform threads of the common `ForkJoinPool`
options.says: The page says parallel streams run on the platform threads of the common ForkJoinPool.

options.text: On platform threads of a `ThreadPoolExecutor` per stream
options.says: The page names one shared pool, the common ForkJoinPool, not an executor made for each stream.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the API contract of `Collectors.toList()` promise about the list it returns?

options.text: That it is a mutable `ArrayList`, so adding to it is safe
options.says: The page says the JDK happens to return an ArrayList, but the contract promises neither that type nor mutability.

options.text: That it is unmodifiable, just like `Stream.toList()` gives
options.says: The page contrasts the two: Stream.toList() is the one documented as unmodifiable.

options.text: Neither its concrete type nor whether it may be changed
options.says: The page says the contract guarantees neither the type nor the mutability, and names Collectors.toCollection(ArrayList::new) for a list you must change.

concepts: Collectors.toList() promises neither the type nor the mutability of the list it returns.
Parallel streams run on the platform threads of the common ForkJoinPool, not on virtual threads.
